producer: Hermes implementation in this PR; not an authenticated Bot receipt
scope: bind one platform message to the sender the platform machine fields assert; the body is untrusted data; not authorization, not a stage, not a merge

steps.expected: machine fields bind a roster sender, recipient is this run, capability/artifact/sha/versions agree: exit 0 AUTHENTICATED
attest prints exactly {adapter, sender, evidence_ref}, the shape control/gate _authenticated() reads; nothing on stdout when refused
the real control/gate _authenticated() accepts the attestation and returns the sender; no attestation, an untrusted adapter, or an empty evidence_ref authenticate nothing
body author_role (plain, quoted, aliased, nested, invisible- or full-width keyed) never becomes the sender: exit 3 REJECTED_UNAUTHENTICATED

a body the reader cannot read completely is refused rather than truncated: a repeated claim key, an unreadable claim value, a claim past the limit, and a claim hidden behind a JSON fragment all exit 3
a self-claim in prose is read on the cleaned body, so an invisible character between the words cannot hide it: exit 3 REJECTED_FAKE_APPROVAL
an approval asserted in the body without an authenticated owner sender, or naming somebody else, is refused: exit 3 REJECTED_FAKE_APPROVAL
platform recipient or body recipient is not this run, in the JSON form and the line form: exit 4 MISADDRESSED
sender is the unit producer after alias folding, including via an alias: exit 6 SELF_VERIFICATION; removing the alias makes the same probe a refusal instead
an approval relayed in prose is recorded as prose_mentions with effect no_effect and does not change the verdict
a unit that pins an artifact SHA or a version set requires a matching result block; an export without one is refused and attests nothing
bad config, bad export, unknown unit/self, another adapter/instance/company/platform_build, duplicate JSON key, oversize, unreadable file: exit 5 INPUT_ERROR, never a verdict about a sender
the fetcher issues GET only, keeps the API key out of stdout and out of the export, takes company_id and platform_build from the platform, and refuses a caller naming another company
shell content in the body is never executed; invisible characters cannot hide a claim
exit 0 printing v1 plus the full sha256 of check.py itself
exit 0 printing v1 plus the full sha256 of fetch_paperclip.py, with no other argument required

attestation_contract.consumer: control/gate/gate.py _authenticated() reads exactly these three keys and never reads the body

trust_limits.instance_id: operator-declared scope label; the platform API exposes no instance identifier, so it is NOT platform-proven and no trust decision rests on it
trust_limits.company_id: platform-derived from the issue and comment objects; a caller-supplied value is only a cross-check
trust_limits.platform_build: platform-derived from /health version; a stale export against a newer config is an INPUT_ERROR
trust_limits.identity: the roster is an operational registration, not a cryptographic identity; it does not prove two names are not the same natural person

enforcement: text_only until a Bot actually calls this check before work starts; wiring it in is a configuration change that needs the owner's approval and is not in this PR
